title: The Thyroid That Ran Hot, Then Cold — Ishida PD-1 Discovery, Nivolumab 5C4 Patent & Fab Interface (PDB 5WT9), Biphasic Destructive Thyroiditis vs. Central Hypophysitis, Biotin Assay Interference & Adrenal-First Cortisol Rule

teenKit.tldr: In 15 seconds: Cancer immunotherapy antibodies like nivolumab unlock T cells by blocking PD-1 (PDB 5WT9), sometimes causing the thyroid to spill stored hormone ('run hot') before burning out ('run cold')—while biotin supplements and hidden adrenal insufficiency set dangerous diagnostic traps.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Giving thyroid hormone before checking cortisol in a checkpoint-inhibitor patient with pituitary inflammation can trigger fatal adrenal crisis, and over-the-counter biotin can fake Graves-like thyroid labs.
keyTakeaways: Nivolumab binds the N-terminal loop and FG/BC loops of PD-1 (PDB 5WT9), preventing tumor PD-L1 from shutting down cytotoxic T cells.
Immune-checkpoint destructive thyroiditis is biphasic: damaged follicles first leak preformed T4/T3 (thyrotoxicosis) and weeks later collapse into hypothyroidism.

High-dose biotin interferes with streptavidin-biotin immunoassays, and morning cortisol/ACTH must always be verified before starting levothyroxine lest occult central adrenal insufficiency precipitate crisis.

vocab.meaning: An inhibitory checkpoint receptor on T cells targeted by nivolumab and pembrolizumab.
Painless release of stored thyroid hormone from inflamed follicles followed by hormone depletion and hypothyroidism.
Lab artifact where excess dietary biotin blocks streptavidin capture, falsely lowering sandwich TSH and falsely raising competitive free T4.

quiz.question: Why must clinicians rule out adrenal insufficiency before treating suspected hypothyroidism in a patient on checkpoint blockade?
options: Levothyroxine accelerates cortisol clearance and can precipitate acute adrenal crisis if ACTH/cortisol reserve is missing
Cortisol blocks PD-1 antibodies from binding T cells
Thyroid hormone causes false-positive biotin tests
quiz.explanation: Checkpoint inhibitors can cause hypophysitis (low ACTH and TSH); replacing thyroid hormone alone speeds metabolic clearance of scarce cortisol and triggers adrenal crisis.
